newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Merle Oberon emerald necklace fetches $2 million.
newsitem.headline: Merle Oberon emerald necklace fetches $2 million.

text.p: A magnificent emerald and diamond necklace, made by Cartier and worn by the late exotic British film star Merle Oberon, fetched 2.6 million Swiss francs ($2 million) Tuesday, auction houses said.
The Indian-style necklace, a masterpiece of the French jeweller, was among nearly 600 Cartier works sold jointly by Geneva's Antiquorum Auctioneers and the Parisian Etude Tajan.

An Oriental-style gold "mystery clock," resembling a temple gate and set with jade and mother-of-pearl in a shining example of Cartier's Art Deco period, went for 1.8 million Swiss francs ($1.4 million).
"The sale has been a great success overall. We are more than satisfied," auctioneer chairman Jacques Tajan told Reuters. "Many lots went for two or three times their pre-sale estimate."
The total figure for the Cartier sale -- marred by the theft in Milan, Italy, last Friday of a Kashmir sapphire and diamond bracelet from the jeweller's Art Deco period -- was not yet available.
The bracelet, which belonged to an American family and whose value was estimated at $2 million, was stolen while on view in a Milan hotel -- the last stop of an eight-city world tour.
"We have no news about it, but the police are on the case," said Tajan, who conducted the sale jointly with Antiquorum founder and chairman Osvaldo Patrizzi. "It was bad luck."
The necklace made for Oberon in 1938, set with 29 baroque emerald drops, had been estimated to go for $1.5 million. The identity of the buyer was not immediately disclosed.

Oberon, a Eurasian of Irish descent who lived in Tasmania and India before settling in England where she struggled as a dance-hall hostess and bit-part movie actress, was famous for her exotic beauty and dazzling collection of jewels.
Married to director Alexander Korda, who discovered her, she starred opposite Douglas Fairbanks, Maurice Chevalier and Laurence Olivier in major films of the 1930s.
Jewels and watches by Cartier went for higher than their estimates, with bidders keen to secure a piece of history.
A pair of Art Deco diamond hoop earrings soared to 200,000 Swiss francs ($150,000) -- more than three times their estimate.
The one-day sale was billed as a world premiere, with Cartier offering certificates of authenticity to the new owners as part of its "Fight Against Forgeries."

"Their pitch is credible. They are selling the history of the firm. It is one of the first opportunities to purchase this type of 20th Century artifact," Edward Faber, a dealer on New York's Fifth Avenue, told Reuters in the auction room.
Prototype Cartier watches from limited editions went for several times their pre-sale estimate, according to Teresi.
A 1996 pink gold digital gentleman's wristwatch, from a limited series of three by Cartier for this event and estimated to fetch between $12,000 and $15,000, soared to $75,000.
"The new prototype watches did extremely well," Faber said.
A gold Chinese clock designed as a pagoda, made by Cartier in 1989 and set with 2,471 diamonds, 55 emeralds and other gems, found no new owner. It had been estimated at $650,000 to $750,000.
Later in the evening, Christie's was offering a Bulgari gold necklace worn by Sharon Stone in the film "Casino" and other dazzling designer gems belonging to a jet-set Lebanese divorcee.

The sale of the personal collection of Mouna al-Ayoub, the glamorous Lebanese former wife of Saudi businessman Nasser Al-Rachid, is expected to fetch between $8 million and $10 million, according to Christie's.
The mother of five, who is parting with 146 lots, viewed the collection in Geneva at the weekend, but has since returned to see her children in Saudi Arabia, according to Christies.
"The sale looks very good because there has been strong interest in her jewels. We hope to sell 100 per cent of the lots," a spokeswoman told Reuters.
"She will be giving part of the proceeds to a certain number of foundations and medical institutes in Europe and the United States," she added, declining to give details.
A Bulgari three-row beaded necklace, matching bracelet and pair of earrings -- worn by Stone in Martin Scorsese's film "Casino" last year -- is estimated to go for $10,000 to $15,000.
